detection_evidence: Section 1: 'we built an agent-based simulation (ABS) of consumers and firms connected through a social network'

deliberate_gaps.derivation: Section 5.4 lists four assumptions but gives no justification for any of them; ABS-supp 3.4 requires authors to 'state and justify the assumptions'.

Section 6.1 gives the initial population, states, attributes, network and declares initialisation stochastic, but nowhere states whether a warm-up period was used (ABS-supp 4.1: 'State if a warm-up period has been used').

Section 7.4 says only 'Hardware specification: not applicable for a model of this size.' No run time and no hardware are given, and no justification beyond model size is offered. Rule R17: 5.4 is never automatically Not applicable; the correct outcome is Missing (low impact for a small model) or, at minimum, Not applicable flagged as 'no justification given'. The audit must not accept the author's N/A claim silently.

justified_not_applicable.evidence: Section 4.5 Entry / exit: 'no agents are created or destroyed, so rules for agent entry and exit are not applicable to this model'
Section 3: 'We did not test theories, run a designed experiment, or use simulation optimisation'

unjustified_not_applicable_claims.claim: Section 7.4: 'Hardware specification: not applicable for a model of this size.'
unjustified_not_applicable_claims.expected_handling: not accepted as N/A; reported as Missing (or N/A with 'no justification given'), citing R17/R1

cross_reference_expectations.1.3 <-> 2.3: consistent (L0/L1 in section 3; section 4.3 states the only difference)
cross_reference_expectations.4.3/5.2 <-> 3.3: consistent: stochastic model (6.3), distributions in 5.3, PCG64 and seeds in 7.2
cross_reference_expectations.5.3 <-> 5.1: consistent: Mesa scheduler described; versions given

notes: 2.5 parent is Addressed because every applicable sub-item (2.5.1-2.5.3) is Addressed and 2.5.4 is a justified N/A. 6.1 is Addressed by a repository plus an archive DOI (fictional).
